noise.note: R broad (4 cells), G middle (12), B fine (32); 0..1 values, mean 0.5

strip.border_band.note: alpha 1 at the border edge, 0 inside

strip.foam.note: the foam line just off the shore

zoom.note: A piece is drawn at scale = (r / base_radius_px) * band.scale_mul[family]. Bands are picked by the hex radius r in screen px: the first band with r >= r_min.

ground.note: Sample every cover texture in world space: uv = world_px_at_base_radius / texture_world_px, so neighbouring hexes share the pattern and no seam shows. Multiply by level_tint[level], then the relief shade (WorldCover.shade). Blend (the owner's narrow v2 blend: hexes still read as hexes): at a pixel, e = its distance in r units to the nearest edge of its hex, signed + inside; the hex and the neighbour across that edge mix with t = smoothstep(-band, band, e + n), n = noise_amp * (noise.r * 2 - 1); near a corner the third hex joins the same way. The noise is sampled in world space (noise_world_px per texture repeat) so both sides of an edge agree.

valley_floor.note: the valley flag is a paler meadow ribbon

scatter.grid: A square world grid over the whole map, not per hex. Point (i, j) sits at (i, j) * step + jitter * step * (h1 - 0.5, h2 - 0.5), odd rows j shifted by half a step in x (so rows do not line up), with h1, h2 two hashes of (layer, i, j) in 0..1. The cover and level at the jittered point come from the hex under it. A third hash below density keeps the point; a fourth picks the species by weight; a fifth picks size and variant. So the result is stable between runs and saves, and a forest runs on across hex edges.

calm.note: no tree, rock or mountain within site_radius of a settlement, castle or hospice site; none within line_clear of a river or road line; no mountain within crest_clear of a crest or pass edge (the crest pieces stand there). The site.calm decal goes under every site (scale 1.0 at a town of level 3).

farmland.note: fields come from the farm rule below

southern.rule: hexes south of lat_max (Liguria, Tuscany) at level <= 3 swap broadleaf for the southern family with this share

snowline.rule: conifers at level >= 5 use the conifer_snow family

mountains.rule: On the mountains grid the kind comes from the height interpolated between the three nearest hex centres (relief levels, inverse-distance weights), so a range fades from snowy peaks to rocky ranges to wooded hills across hex edges.

fields.rule: Parcels stand on the fields grid. Each farm (a farmland hex, or a settlement) spreads parcels round its site out to radius[level] (r units); a point takes the nearest farm in reach. The parcel's angle is the same for all parcels of one farm (a hash of the farm hex, in 0..180 degrees, snapped to 15). Style by weight; terraces replace grain on level >= 3 ground.
fields.farm_level: farmland hex: 1; a settlement of level L also farms its own hex at L and ring 1 at L - 2

sites.site_point: The hex centre, moved a third of a hex away from the hex's river edges (to the dry side), or towards the quay edge for a port; a river city's site is the hex centre.
sites.town: town.<level>.v<hash % 3>, anchor on the site point
sites.capital: town.palace.v0 at site + (0.62, 0.12) r, and label.crown.* on the plate
sites.castle: with a town: castle.<level>.v<hash % 2> at site + (-0.6, 0.2) r; alone: on the site
sites.port: port.quay.<stone for sea and lake | wood for rivers>.d<edge direction of the quay edge>, anchored on that edge's midpoint; port.boat.cog.* on the water off big ports
sites.hospice: site.hospice.v<hash % 2> on the saddle hex centre, site.cairn.v0 at + (0.3, -0.15) r

edges.direction_order: 0 E, 1 NE, 2 NW, 3 W, 4 SW, 5 SE (WorldGrid.neighbour); corner k at -90 + 60k degrees
edges.crest: relief.crest.<orientation>.<snow if both hexes are level 6 or either is snow cover, else rock>.v<hash % 2>, anchor on the edge midpoint. Lit pieces are never rotated or mirrored.
edges.cap: relief.cap.<snow|rock>.v<hash>, on every corner where two or more crest edges meet
edges.cliff: coast.cliff.d<direction from the land hex to the sea>.v<hash % 2>, on the edge midpoint (also step = scarp, facing the lower hex)
edges.beach: coast.beach.d<direction>: optional; the coastline recipe draws the rim (D7)
edges.bridge: road.bridge.<stone|wood|ford|ferry>.axis<a>: a = 0 for a road crossing an E/W edge, 1 for NE/SW, 2 for NW/SE; on the river edge's midpoint. crossing bridge_stone -> stone, bridge_wood -> wood

border.style: A (D6): a band of the country colour inside the border, a dark line on it, a faint wash
border.draw_order: band and wash under the upright objects; the line above them (reads through forests)

lines.note: Rivers and roads are drawn as strips (geometry). Widths in r units, with a floor in px.
